name: AWS EC2 Spot for GPU: the 90% ceiling is real but the per-SKU rate is not published in one place
region: all AWS commercial regions; rate varies by Availability Zone
price_basis: NO SINGLE SPOT price_usd, deliberately, and the basis is stated as a CEILING not a rate. AWS states Spot is 'available at a discount of up to 90% off compared to On-Demand pricing' and that 'Spot Instance prices are set by Amazon EC2 and adjust gradually based on long-term trends in supply and demand'. The page's own table 'displays the Spot price for each region and instance type (updated every 5 minutes)' but states 'The prices displayed below are the lowest prices per instance type in the region' - so even the rendered grid is a FLOOR per instance type, not a per-AZ rate, and the per-AZ numbers live behind the Spot Instance pricing history page. Spot price history is only reachable through the describe-spot-price-history API. The concrete On-Demand anchors these discounts apply to, read out of the EC2 Price List API us-east-1 file with publicationDate 2026-09-25: p5.48xlarge (8x H100 SXM) $55.04/instance-hour; p5.4xlarge (1x H100 SXM) $6.88; p5en.48xlarge (8x H200) $63.296; p4de.24xlarge (8x A100 80GB) $27.44705; p4d.24xlarge (8x A100) $21.957642; g6e.48xlarge (8x L40S) $30.13118; g6e.xlarge (1x L40S) $1.861; g6.48xlarge (8x L4) $13.3504; g4dn.12xlarge (4x T4) $3.912. PER-GPU-HOUR, derived: H100 SXM $6.88, H200 $7.912, A100 80GB $3.4309, L40S $3.7664, L4 $1.6688.
notes:
THREE THINGS THAT MAKE 'UP TO 90% OFF' UNUSABLE AS A BUDGET NUMBER. (1) It is a ceiling across ALL EC2 SKUs, not an H100 figure; nobody has ever paid 90% off for p5. (2) The published grid is the LOWEST price per instance type in the region, so budgeting off it understates what you will actually pay in a specific AZ, and GPUs are the SKUs where per-AZ spread is widest because capacity is lumpy. (3) There is no single place on AWS's site where a per-SKU spot rate is stated; the only authoritative source is the describe-spot-price-history API or the Bid Advisor page. The interruption reality from AWS's own documentation: Spot instances are reclaimed on a two-minute warning, and p5/p5en are the SKUs with the deepest demand pools and therefore the worst interruption profile - which is a structural argument, not a measured one. The commitment-discount exclusion is the rule that breaks naive cost models: on Google Cloud the pricing page states explicitly that Spot VMs and preemptible VMs cannot receive CUDs or SUDs. Never model a spot instance as also earning a commitment discount. Related existing records: aws-ec2-spot-gpu-general for the structural picture, aws-ec2-p5-h100 and aws-ec2-p5en-h200 for the on-demand anchors.

 EXPORT CONTROL (2026-10-04, mechanism-level; sources spl-bis-2026-05-d5-guidance, spl-bis-2026-01-advanced-computing-case-by-case): renting capacity does NOT remove the export-control question, it relocates it. Providing remote access to controlled computing capability can constitute a transfer under the EAR, so the provider must screen the end user; and separately, under the 91 FR 1684 licence regime the consignee must run KYC procedures to prevent unauthorized remote access and must manage and limit IaaS access to the hardware - obligations pushed onto the customer, who must be told to implement them. For a customer headquartered or parented in Country Group D:5 or Macau the 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A) end-user/parent test can bite even when the capacity is consumed in a permitted region. Recorded true because the underlying hardware is controlled and the provider carries the screening duty, not because access to a US region is itself restricted.

 LEAD TIME: null, and this is not a gap - for Spot it would be the wrong unit. Spot capacity is reclaimed at any time, so its defining characteristic is that there is no forward commitment available at all: the correct planning figure is the INTERRUPTION rate, not a delivery date, and Azure publishes the corresponding number directly ('Azure will evict Azure Spot Virtual Machines with 30-seconds notice') while GCP states Compute Engine 'might preempt Spot VMs at any time'. Anyone needing a guaranteed week-count should read the on-demand or Capacity Block rates instead; the 8-week maximum Capacity Block booking horizon is documented in source spl-aws-capacity-block-booking-horizon. Probe log in source spl-negative-no-oem-publishes-lead-time.
